issue: In Find mode, pressing u on the search-results screen did not go back to the Find menu: the prompt simply repeated. The abort state it left behind then made the next screen (cheat codes) repaint endlessly and fill the Select prompt with q characters.

On Android (Termux), uploading with up- printed a regex error and then claimed the link was not kept in the cloud, so the link never reached Home > Links. Bash regexes with repeat counts above 255 are rejected by Android's regex engine, which also broke a local key copy and a comment-skipping pattern in switch.

Pasting a long link into a typed-line prompt on a narrow screen printed the prompt and part of the link dozens of times. The line editors redraw in place assuming prompt and text fit on one terminal row, and every wrapped keystroke added a new copy.
After the paste-spam fix, a long pasted link in the free-text prompt scrolled sideways inside a single row and hid most of the text. It should wrap onto following lines like a normal read.

Footers, live suggestions, cheat codes and real key handling disagreed across menus. Examples: b-N buffered items instead of removing them, suggested keys were rejected on Enter, u was accepted as text and a backup ran before the cancel took effect, and c was refused at a prompt that listed it.

Pasting a large paragraph into any menu input was treated as many Enter presses and replayed as a typing animation, and the app slowed badly on big text. A paste should be one input accepted only on Enter at any size, and file or folder names over 255 bytes must be refused with a clear message.
After pastes were flattened to one row, multi-line pasted text became a single clipped line. Line breaks should be kept and the full text shown across wrapped rows.
With a long pasted text shown as one clipped row, pressing Left moved the cursor onto the Select label because the visible text window never scrolled with the cursor.

Add a maximum accepted input length (2000 characters at the time) for every prompt: oversized typing or pastes must be refused with a message and a redraw, including pastes that arrive in several chunks.

Native Google Docs, Sheets and Slides opened from Drive appeared as Office files, and move or copy actions uploaded real or empty Office copies, leaving corrupted files and removing the originals. Google-native files must never be converted or altered by Drive operations, and users need a way to find files already damaged. The gdrive folder also belonged inside the fx tree.

Organising a Google Drive folder by extension created the folders but left them empty and sent every file to the Drive bin, and it took about 300 seconds. Moving files into a folder created in the same sync was treated as delete plus upload.

After an upload of a 115 MB file was interrupted at about 80 MB, resuming from Pending found only about 2 MB safe on the server. Too many large blobs were in flight at once, and each half-sent blob is discarded.
The Pending menu contacted the server without the loading bar that every other networked menu shows, so the screen looked frozen while waiting.
Cutting parallel uploads from 16 to 4 for resilience may slow total upload time. The goal was to keep the original speed and the improved resume safety together.

After upload blobs shrank from 16 MiB to 4 MiB, the backend needed a review for costs that grow with blob count. Found per-object deletes exceeding batch limits, a rate limit that throttles restores, and a browser download that kept less data in flight.
In the Links list, the chosen sort order showed in the header but the rows never reordered after returning from Settings. The redraw after a command-map action bypassed the menu's own sorting.
A pasted text showed only about six rows. Everything pasted, up to the input limit, should be visible.

The caret appeared one cell too far right after typing, although editing behaved correctly. It could not be reproduced in the emulator, so nothing was changed (see BB-211020261500-1 for the later fix).
Typing an item number beyond the list highlighted the last item instead of highlighting nothing.
Deleting a typed number back to empty left the previously highlighted item highlighted.
Lower the maximum accepted input and paste length from 2000 to 512 characters.
Stop searching commands on every keystroke once the typed text passes 56 characters. Longer text is resolved only when Enter is pressed.
Pressing u in a Links screen opened from Home went to Local Surf instead of back to Home.
Pressing q inside fx, switch, rules and other menus quit the whole app instead of returning to the main loop.
The caret was drawn one cell too far right in some prompts, such as the backup confirmation. Two inconsistent character-width tables treated text-default emoji as double width.
Home, Settings and other menus did not show the dim command-suggestion row that the main menu shows while typing.
New main-screen layout: a status row, separate cd path and nav path lines, and the suggestion row above the Select prompt instead of below it.
Replace a fixed set of status and navigation icons with new ones across the app.
The language field in the new status row should show which engine loaded the folder (c or py), not a human language.
The cd path line should show the shell's current directory, but it showed the browsed folder, the same as the nav path line.
Remove all copy-pasted code, including blocks of about ten similar lines, by moving each copy into one shared helper so a later fix cannot miss a duplicate.

The fixed-issue corpus was a flat folder of notes with issues in the reporter's own words, and AGENTS.md did not tell agents to consult it or to reuse and dedupe code. Past fixes were hard to find and match to new symptoms, and new code could drift from existing code.

The copy-paste checker dupscan only matched runs of about ten identical or similarly shaped lines, so it missed duplicate functions that were renamed, reformatted or written in another language. The Polyglot Clone Finder, which parses the code and verifies candidates exactly, was to replace it.

Polyglot had to become a normal Infinity Stones tool that starts and behaves like the JavaScript and Python audits, and its results had to warn that it only finds candidates and is not fully reliable.

The only self-install code (a one-shot pip install guarded by a retry sentinel) lived inside the recents daemon, and polyglot needed the same behaviour for numpy, rich, openpyxl and the tree-sitter grammars. Copying it would have created a second copy that could drift.

Menu footer keys (u) Up, q) Quit, h) Home ...) had no touch or click support, unlike items and headers. They should react to a double tap or double click only, because footers sit next to the prompt and are easy to touch by accident.

While mouse reports are on, the wheel or swipe is always consumed by the menu, so the terminal's own scrollback cannot be reached: the screen above the menu or below it could not be scrolled to, even at the first or last list row or with the touch outside the menu block.
On touch terminals a tap on the Select: row did nothing and the soft keyboard did not open, because mouse reports were on and the tap was reported to the app instead.
The new test 'hand-back ends at the next typed key' in tests/mouse/mouse_test.py fails with prompt 17 instead of 7.

Find & replace in the Find menu (f) only handled names or contents separately and had no "both" mode. Its name search used shell glob semantics, so a pattern such as "hello [c]" matched the wrong files and descended into folders even when only the current folder was meant.

The bash implementation of find & replace was slow on recursive trees and not robust (non-atomic edits, no clash detection, binary and VCS folders touched), and the app had no settings for the choices it offers.
Running the test suite after a small fix took about half an hour, far longer than the fix itself, and agents added their own long sleeps (sleep 600) while waiting for it.
Several tests failed from the start although the app worked, and the agent had to acknowledge the red result and move on.
AGENTS.md made agents run the polyglot duplicate scan, which reads the whole repo and installs packages, on every job, which is slow and rarely useful for ordinary fixes.

Buffers held only flat path lists, and "as <name>" existed only for FileAPI links. Wanted: named sets in every buffer, applied one at a time with d- <name>, shown grouped in v-, a new select buffer feeding the fx *.selected.items actions, and a rule for a set name that is used twice.
_sp_count style helpers printed "0" twice when grep -c found nothing (grep exits 1 after printing 0, then || echo 0 added a second line), breaking numeric tests.

The caret in text prompts that start with an emoji (for example the backup confirmation) can land one cell off on some devices, because terminals and the width table disagree about emoji width. An earlier fix covered only some devices.
Yes/no/cancel questions were one-line prompts such as "[Y/n, c = cancel the delete]:" which look old and do not take touch or click.
Fixed-action prompts such as "c) copy link   g) regenerate link   e) edit expiry   a) alias/rename   x) nuke   Enter) back:" were hand-made one-line key rows.
Radio and checkbox rows looked the same ([x] / [ ]), so a one-of-many choice could not be told from a many-of-many one.

Two agents changed the same base independently: one replaced one-line prompts with the shared choice menu (no emoji on a read line, [o] radio vs [x] checkbox), the other added named buffer sets ("as <name>", k- for shortcut, s- for select, d- <name>, conflict rules, the w prefix in the fx pickers). Their work had to become one version where the new set code follows the new menu rules.

Items staged with a plain s-1,2 (no name) were ignored by the fx <action>.selected.items picker, the cheatcode test still expected the old emoji prompt, and llms-full.txt still called s- the shortcut key.

Menu footers were typed by hand at about 50 _mc_footer call sites, so the generic keys carried drifting labels (u as Back / back / Exit, q as Quit / Close, z as Cancel, rf as Refresh / refresh / Reload) and nothing checked that a footer key was wired in any command map.

Footer labels for the generic keys were still hand-typed in some menus after BB-241020261928-1: case-only variants (u:back, rf:refresh) in the Cloud Surf, notification, RBAM and Cloudflare screens, and the guard that forbids retyping them was case-sensitive.
Every file_fx ADF action repeated its label, its function and a typed tree path (file_fx/<verb>/<label>), and nothing checked that registering files were loaded or that registered functions existed.
The main-command reference lived only in cmd_def lines; 12 commands (.us bk clear fa forceshow gd gdx ns sast scr-sync sn sv) were not named in README, llms*.txt or help.txt.

The CPU-to-binary mapping (uname -m to arm64 / amd64 / arm, and android / linux) existed in _bvk_engine_target and was copied three more times (_bvk_xfer_bin in fileapi_lib, two places in health.sh); the bvk-ls section of health ignored $OSTYPE when detecting Android, unlike the real code.

Loading bars were wired by hand around a few slow calls (api, upgrade, workers, drive profiles, pending, recursive filter), so most waits (replace in files, infinity actions, navigating pn / nf, deleting many items) showed nothing. A bar had to appear for every wait without any call site asking for it.

Settings rows only showed a short label and value, so a person who does not know what a buffer, a nuke time or regex is could pick an option that is wrong for their use. Every setting needed a long plain-words explanation above the suggestion row.
Delete-type confirmations had "No" as the default answer, so a bare Enter silently answered them. They should have no default: the person must answer.

Merging the v1a and v1b branches (BB-251020262145-1..3 and BB-241020261928-1, BB-241020262040-1..4) broke Settings screens that are sourced on their own: settings_ui.sh called _st_desc_prepare, which lives in settings_desc.sh that only the import file loads, so the harness of tests/stale_size and the main-header check of tests/hints failed with an arithmetic error and a missing header.

The Settings description block (BB-251020262145-2) changed height with the highlighted row (a long text, a short text, none), so each redraw moved the prompt up or down a row and left a blank row under it; the mouse wheel on the last screen row was then handed back to the terminal (tests/mouse "wheel on the prompt row stays with the menu" failed).

The loading bar of BB-251020262145-1 scrolled the whole screen up by one line whenever it appeared while the cursor was on the last screen row (for example the "Starting" bar on a slow start): the top header row was pushed off the screen and stayed lost.

Tests relied on the old loading bar's output as a side effect: tests/mouse tab_click returned as soon as the harness saw 0.2 s of silence, and the -u screen is silent for about half a second while it fetches tags, so the tap on the second tab was read from a half-painted screen; tests/choose read the screen right after the title appeared, before the rows were drawn.

Generic footer keys (u q z rf) were still hand-typed at about 20 call sites with labels that drift (u:Exit, q:Close, rf:Reload, u:cancel, u:up/back, u:Up parent, u:Remove last prefix) and in registered footers (u:Up, q:Quit, rf:Refresh_Drive), and the guard of BB-241020262040-1 only matched the exact canonical spelling in quoted items.

bashbasicsbyvk_adf_recover.sh registered an ADF action but no import file loads it (BB-241020262040-2 found it and listed it as "known legacy" in tests/adf_registry.sh), and switch.sh _sw_excl_add still printed a hand-made 1-4 list.

Delete-type confirmations: BB-251020262145-3 fixed 13 call sites by hand, but about ten more destructive questions still defaulted to "No" (clear buffer x4, free downloaded Drive content, remove stale registry entries, overwrite x2, "Are you really sure?" when removing users, and the shared _xui_yes used for Nuke / Remove / Revoke), and any new one would again.

The Home screen (15 rows) and the Pending FileAPI actions screen (8 rows) had no description although AGENTS rule 8 and BB-251020262145-2 say every Settings screen and row has one, and nothing checked it.
v1a (smart loading bar, Settings descriptions) shipped no tests, and v1b added tests only for its own changes, so the merge had no guard for either feature.

A GitHub management feature was wanted inside fx: one ADF button that signs in with a key already on the machine (or explains where to put one), lists all repos, and for a repo manages Stable releases and Tags (create, edit title / notes / tag message / commit message, rename with conflict checks, delete, download = clone with or without depth), singly and in bulk.
The upgrade loop carried its own copies of the release-list parser, the commit parser, the tag ordering pipeline and the body printer, which the new GitHub screens also needed.

In fx -> github_fx -> open github, typing a command the footer shows (d, e, r, c, g, rf, d-1 ...) answered "not available here - Enter will cancel" / "Invalid command: d - not available in xui". Footer, command map, hint and cheat code disagreed. A user also reported stray text ("[C", "[<0;44;37M") on the repo screen after the right key / a tap.

Six menu maps (find, home, organise, settings, snapshot, transfer) wired 50 main-list commands each (sw fx api bk cd c d r ... kl) as usable, tagged "AUTO: loop not analysed", so the hint row and cc advertised commands those screens have no case arm for. Follow-up of BB-201020260325-1 (same family: footer, map, hint, cc and real handling must agree).

On the Settings and Home screens (and every other _st_run list screen called without a cmd_fn) a typed main command did nothing: h s i -h -auth disk ram health lang sast were cleared silently, although the hint row, cc and the map listed them as available. Blocked keys were also cleared without any note.

Merge of v1a (GitHub screens, shared ghlib, command-gate and block() map change) and v1b (smartload, Settings descriptions, no-default deletes, generated-list tests) into one tree; the GitHub screens had to be ported to the v1b engine rules (no _lb_run, bare footer keys, -d none, _sl_hold around git progress).

Agents ran the fast tier, then the full suite, then reruns after every edit, even when only a comment, description, header, footer or command code changed. The tests cost minutes and tokens and cannot fail on such an edit. AGENTS.md only said "run the tests that cover what you touched" with no minor-change exemption, and agents other than those reading AGENTS.md never saw it.

After tests ran the agent could use up the whole usage budget inside the test loop, so the owner received no output until the limit reset. The test tiers were also not tied to the size of the change, the runner capped parallelism at 4 jobs and started slow tests last, and tests/github/ui_test.py failed whenever the machine had GH_TOKEN set.

When the input of a list screen (Settings, Home, choose menus) was gone (tty closed, SSH link dropped, tmux pane killed), the screen never left: a failed read was turned into the typed character q, over and over, so the prompt filled with q and the shell burned CPU. Follow-up of BB-201020260021-1 (same symptom, other cause).

On a list screen the arrows, the wheel and a row tap put the row number on the Select line. The next typed character was appended to it: Down then 5 gave 15, Down then h gave 3h (which Enter then cleared without doing anything).

Typing a row number that does not exist (15 of 12 rows) left the highlight on the row of the first digit, and Space then toggled that row; erasing the typed number with Backspace left its row highlighted and Enter on the empty line opened it. Same family as BB-211020260830-3 and BB-211020260830-4, which fixed only the main menu and the smart menus.
A text + Enter that arrived in one piece was refused when it was too large or came out empty, but its Enter was still queued, so whatever had been typed before it (a row number) was opened.

bashbasicsbyvk_mapgen wired the dash keys s- do- snap- (and c- m- on some menus) as usable on menus whose loop has no arm for them, only because the loop body contains a bare s (a printf %s) or the word do (every while ... do). Follow-up of BB-251020260246-1, which left the "loop mentions it" branch open.
_st_readkey skipped a mouse release by calling itself, one nested call per ignored report.
Review claim: pasted text on a list screen is not sanitized, so a CR, tab or ESC byte reaches the line and garbles the row.
Review claim: _CM_ACT is not cleared before _cm_resolve in _st_cm_gate, so a stale run could fire on unknown text.
Review claims: a footer tap or row click leaves the =filter on, so u clears the filter instead of going back; s on Settings and h on Home open a second copy of the screen.
The smart loading bar was drawn on the row below the cursor, leaving an empty row between the typed command and the bar. It should be drawn on the cursor row, in the cursor's place.
The loading bar kept animating after nano (a full-screen editor) was opened, drawn in the middle of nano's own screen. A full-screen program is not a wait.

Typing cd with a full path at the main prompt (for example into storage/dcim/Camera) did nothing visible: no folder change, no bar, no clear error. cd is only a bare command in the app, so the line is refused as an invalid selection; a hang on a real device could not be reproduced.

A transfer's own progress bar (percent, x of n MB, speed, ETA, pending count) stopped showing in every fileapi service (upload, backup, saved, snapshot, ux share, download): since smartload draws a loading bar for every wait, the loading bar replaced the progress bar, which was only visible in v115. The two bars were never kept apart; when both want the row, the progress bar must win.
The loading bar appeared after 0.2 s of quiet, so it flashed up for ordinary short waits; it should appear only after 2 s.

Archive support covered only zip and tar.gz and recognised an archive by the last dot of its name, so copies such as hello.zip1, hello_tar.gz, hello.tar-1.gz or "hello- (2).zip" were refused. Nine formats are wanted: zip, tar, tar.gz/tgz, tar.xz/txz, tar.bz2/tbz2, 7z, tar.zst/tzst, tar.lz4 and .skill.

The file menu (handle_file) always said Run for an archive, had separate Lock and Unlock rows, and lacked Copy Name, Copy File Path and Go To Parent Folder. The main-loop lang command ignored the find and replace engine, and there was no command to jump to a typed path.

External dependencies were handled by many separate, private bootstrappers (pipboot, polyglot_bootstrap, the daemon's pip call, gitpush's gh installer, timezone's package table, archive tool tables) and by "X not found, install it with ..." messages that exited. A missing tool should instead open one Installer menu (list, yes/no) driven by one central registry of dependencies and of which menu needs what.

On Termux, extracting an archive printed an invalid regular expression (empty (sub)expression) from bashbasicsbyvk_archive_formats.sh: the copy-marker stripping of the archive stem used an empty alternative (x|), which glibc accepts and Termux's regcomp rejects.

Settings and Home screens showed the highlighted row's description in a padded block under the footer, with extra footer text; wanted the screen text in the header, a short footer without gaps, and a tappable Settings part in the path.
A gzip stream holding a tar but named without the word tar (3bvk_full.gz) was refused by uz-1 because only the name was checked before the content.
Yes/no menus carried a default answer (-u asked Continue? with No highlighted); wanted: no yes/no question has any default.
Settings and Home screens needed a blank line under the description and no extra blank rows under the footer when no suggestion is shown.

A script started from the file menu's Run (run_file) kept the smartload wait open for its whole run: the loading bar drew over the script's own prompt, with a timer counting up, and the script's output could not wipe it. Wanted: a bar only for the few seconds between launching a script and its first paint, none inside the script.

The loading bar showed after only 0.2 s of waiting and also for plain value flips (Left / Right / Space / click on a settings row), so it flashed on nearly every action. The header, the tests and the VK_SMARTLOAD_GRACE_MS note all say 2 s.
A line typed into a read -s prompt went through the text-prompt read shim, and its text became the loading bar's label ("Working on <typed text>") on a long wait.

Prebuilt engines (bvk-ls, bvk-fr, bvk-xfer) were only produced for linux and android on amd64, arm64 and arm. Wanted in addition: darwin-amd64, darwin-arm64, linux-386 and freebsd-amd64, found and used by the app like the others.

`pip install` put every prebuilt binary (18) into the install dir, so on Termux the browser listed all of them, and the wheel was tagged py3-none-any, so pip could reuse a wheel built for one CPU / OS on another. Nothing noticed or repaired an install that was carried to a different machine.

The smartload loading bar was left out for waits that should have had one: a silent helper (python, node, a Go engine) that was only computing got no bar, because any non-listed child holding the terminal on stdin, stdout or stderr counted as its owner. Whether a bar showed depended on whether the call site happened to redirect stderr.

The loading bar's delay was inconsistent: 2 s for Enter, 4 s for Left / Right / Space / click (even where Space / click run the same command as Enter, settings_ui _st_activate) and 1 s for a program's start-up. The same action behaved differently depending on the key, and anything under 2 s, or any job that printed more often than every 2 s, never showed a bar.

When a bar appeared there was no way to tell why: its label was only "Working" for a menu pick (the smart menu passed just the row token), and nothing recorded which Enter opened the wait, who closed it, why an Enter opened none (subshell, hold) or which child muted the bar.

`o` sourced about 130 library files (1.45 MB) through eight import files before the first paint, although the first screen calls only a fraction of them; the first paint waited for all of it (about 2 s on a phone). Wanted: one file that says per file whether it loads before the first paint, after it, or never until called, and a rule that every future file goes through it.

Typing print (or cc, loadtime, settings) at a plain text prompt such as the rename New name line, leaving that command's menu with u or q, left a smartload Working bar on the prompt row while it waited for input; _cm_text_read closed the wait once, not on every redraw of the prompt.

The one-by-one rename screen was an old two-line prompt. It is now a Settings-style Rename screen with description, item list, footer, suggestions and Old / New lines; Up or a tap on Old copies the old name; long selections go to the CSV rename (limit in Settings > Rename); a new name without an extension follows Settings > Rename > No extension.

Suggestion (cheat code) rows were cut with an ellipsis when longer than one row. They now expand onto more rows, like a Settings description, in the main menu, Settings and every text prompt (_bvk_hint_wrap).

Merged v1a (load mapper) and v1b (rename screen, text-prompt bar fix, wrapping suggestions) into one tree; v1b's renamesettings.sh registered in the load mapper because the import file it was added to no longer exists.

Opening a folder with a .shortcut file printed '_shortcut_read_field: command not found' (displayer.sh lines 947-949): the load mapper sourced its stubs after the first paint, but the first paint calls functions of lazily loaded files. The stubs are now sourced at the end of the [fg] step.

Rename is one screen: title, description, items, 'u) Up   q) Close', a 'Select:' prompt, then Old / New under it for each chosen item (it was a picker screen plus a second screen that drew the list again).
New Settings > System > Nano text wrap (wrap | no wrap); the choice is written to nanorc as one managed block that is replaced on every change, also by Import nano settings.

New command eb-<items> (eb-1-5): exact bytes per item and in total, in binary (KiB) and data (KB) units, then save in Excel (CSV if openpyxl is missing) or copy to the clipboard; reuses the list's cached sizes, wc -c and du -sb.
kl, rf, disk, ram, health, lang, clear, sast, i, -h and -auth are no longer blocked in any menu: kl and rf are now util commands runnable from every screen (rf redraws outside the main list).

New main commands were wanted: xtr- (extract lines, words, characters or bytes from files, files only, with first / range / last / random / duplicate / unique modes and a size unit for bytes) and i- (file info for several files, files only). Both must print their result before offering copy or Excel, like eb-.

A command typed into a plain text question (s, h, cc ... at "Enter folder names", "New:") ran, but when the question was asked again the screen that owned it was not drawn: the output of the command (Settings) stayed on screen with only the prompt under it.

i-N (info of a version, a rule, a release) printed its text and then left a bare "Select:" under it: the menu was not drawn again, only the prompt came back. The info screen was wanted to end with "Press any key to exit info mode" and then hand back to the menu.

The shared-link viewer page (0002-fileapi, page.js) showed "Download failed: decryption error" for every tar.gz archive upload made with up- when its Download all button was pressed in a browser, although do- from the CLI opened the same link. The error text was shown for every kind of failure, so it pointed at the encryption instead of the real cause.

The chunk size and the number of parallel streams of up-, do- and the pending resume were fixed by the program (4 MB pieces, up to 16 streams, 8 for downloads). A setting was wanted where the person picks 4 MB x 64, 8 MB x 32, 16 MB x 16 (recommended) or custom numbers, with a description of who each choice suits, and with hard limits so absurd numbers cannot be used.
The worker accepted any declared transfer shape and had no stated limit for chunk size, streams or blob count, which matters once the person can choose them.

The "==" deep filter existed only in the folder lists (it searches the sub-folders). Settings, Home and the other screens built on the _st_run engine had the live "=" filter of their own rows but no deep search: typing "==" there filtered for a literal "=".

run_file read the first line of any file into a bash variable, so a binary printed 'ignored null byte in input' when the person answered No to the executable prompt; and a No on an executable binary then copied it to Download and tried to open it in another app.
Shebangs with env (#!/usr/bin/env python3, env -S, env NAME=value) ran 'env file'; CRLF shebangs named an interpreter with a trailing carriage return.
run_file launched a bare file name from PATH instead of the current folder, and a file whose whole name was an extension word (a file called py) ran as that language.
dart ran the script twice when it exited non-zero, and .kts scripts were compiled to a jar like .kt files.
force_share built invalid commands (termux-share -c file, am --stream, a string STREAM extra) and a failed share popped a second share sheet; force_open reported success when am failed.
handle_file spun forever on 'invalid' when stdin closed; nano had no fallback; run_file ignored u/q on its yes/no questions; action, yn, classname, tmp, out and mimetype leaked as globals.
The compile-and-run branches (c, c++, rust, swift, haskell) each built a temp binary by hand, and two copies existed of the MIME lookup and the 'less or cat' pager choice.

The file menu's Run asked up to two yes/no questions (run directly, run with the shebang interpreter) before running a file, although the person had already chosen Run and the file's own nature decides the way.
Start-up spent about 450 ms of a 2,133 ms launch on process spawns (uname, mktemp, rm, stty, stat, cat, sha1sum) and the native-engine probe ran again on every call because it ran inside $(...).
The CI step 'Verify one wheel per machine type' failed: every case of tests/engine_target.sh answered amd64.

Every start launched bvk-ls twice more (count and the 'group' check) as a self-test, about 90 ms on the phone, and the folder-size job, two listings of browse.sh and the time zone check each spawned mktemp / rm / date.

A start of o showed nothing for about a second (1,304 ms on the phone, of which only about 200 ms were process launches; the rest is bash loading its functions and building the rows), so the app felt slow however many processes were removed.

Row measuring was the biggest left-over of the first paint: _vp_cells looked at every character of every row one by one because each row has an emoji icon and so never took the ASCII shortcut; 'prepare rows' took 268 ms of its own time on the phone.

After the first speed-up the build list still ran mktemp and rm on every start, and the engine probe still cost 55 ms: the temp folder name was inherited through the environment from an earlier session and pointed to a folder that no longer existed, and $(command -v ...) forked a subshell three times.

The first-screen cache (BB-011120261900-4: o painted the last saved screen of the folder before the real first paint and replaced it) made the screen flicker at start, which the owner did not want, so it was removed.
The rf command left a loading bar that kept animating over the new shell and could not be closed; any exec of a new program from the app that skipped the loading-bar shutdown did the same.
The lang command printed three plain engine lines; it now shows an ENGINE LANGUAGE MATRIX box (C, BASH, PYTHON, GO, NODE columns with PRIMARY, FALLBACK and CURRENT per engine).
The info emoji was replaced by the scroll emoji in the file info screen and in the find & replace skipped-files notes.

The Functions screen (ADF and UDF tabs) had a different header and footer from the other menus, showed the old tab icons, and its Admin Defined folders carried an _fx suffix (file_fx, github_fx, cloudflare_fx, google_drive_fx). Wanted: a title, a tab row with the active tab in brackets, a one-line description, an "X out of N here, T total" line, an "ADF path:" / "UDF path:" line, and one shared footer (u up, q quit, h home, cc cheat codes); the folder names without the suffix.

The -auth user screen lacked View balance and Download ledger rows, and recharge accepted US dollars only. Wanted: both rows, INR payments (Razorpay UPI) with US$1 = 100 INR = 1,000 credits kept in one source of truth on each side.
Remove legacy accounts; diseps 270, dinons 290, apikey 512 chars, d3 renamed d30 (30 codes).
.d.ext py -r ignored -r; .d now supports recursive display as a flat list with relative paths.

Menus with tabs (sw, rule book, upgrade, rbam, cloud surf, a GitHub repo) still used the old header (title and tab bar on one line with a "←/→ tabs" hint, a long footer of command keys), while fx had the newer layout. Each menu also kept its own copy of the tab bar, tab stepping, in-place redraw and viewport setup, so a look change meant editing seven files.

Upload and other transfer receipts each had their own long layout (many lines, abuse/privacy notes, 'gone at' dates). Separately, in headless terminals the upload link was not reaching the clipboard via OSC52, and the 'up-' action felt slow with most of the time hidden from loadtime.

Selection-review menu of the transfer navigator drew its c/x/u/q footer inside the body, and q redrew the navigator (slow listing, repeated prompt) instead of leaving. Find & replace settings were inline one-line questions instead of numbered menus.

One shared text-edit template for every typed-input place: Shift/Ctrl+arrows selection, Ctrl+A, Delete, cut / copy / paste, word delete, undo, with Ctrl-C / Ctrl-Z caught by a signal trap because bash read -n1 never delivers them as bytes.

In Find and Find & replace, u left the whole option sequence (Where?, Match case?, Pattern type?, text prompts, preview, CSV picker) and landed on the Find menu or the main file list instead of going one question back. Follow-up of BB-201020260021-1.

u at a nested prompt cancelled the whole flow (muted) instead of going one step back: rename New:, create, organise, extract and Find text prompts. u now cancels only that prompt and each flow returns to the question or menu before it.

Transfer wizard, delete-by-date and archive left the flow on u instead of going one step back; navigator footer keys u) Up and z) Cancel were not honoured (u left the transfer, z was refused); default-on-Enter prompts took the default on u.

In a few small menus (Cloudflare workers/pages recover, Google Drive profiles, Cloud Surf people and file tree, Rbam person) the screen's own keys were rejected as 'Invalid command ... not available in xui' and rf did not reload, because these _xui_loop screens had no command map and silently inherited the generic xui one. In yes/no and choice boxes a typed command was shown in the hint row but dropped on Enter (the cmd_fn swallowed every word). Plain word = command, @word = text now holds there; a test fails when a screen has no map.

A bookmark of a file opened the parent folder in the main list instead of acting as a pointer to the file. Wanted: a file bookmark opens the same run loop the file gets in the local view; Recents follows the same rule.

Bookmark rows showed a generic page emoji and the internal .swlink suffix instead of what the same item shows in the local list. Wanted: one shared emoji table for local view, Recents, Bookmarks and Favourites, bookmarks without the suffix and with the target's lock mark.

Renaming or moving a bookmarked item left its bookmark pointing at the old path; the daemon only followed favourites and a list of modified files and knew nothing about bookmarks, and its polling fallback could not see renames. Wanted: every pointer to a path (bookmarks, recents, favourites, locks, shortcuts) follows renames, moves and deletes.
Recents was every file the daemon saw modified, read-only, files only. Wanted: folders entered with the in-app cd and files edited in the run loop only, with automatic locking after more than 5 uses.

The recents daemon and the snapshot daemon each had their own single-instance, pid, log, lock and version code, scattered over several folders. They now share one helper (planetary resources), live in script/file/daemons and are called the local daemon and the alien daemon.

Pointer upkeep after a move or delete outside the app could lose or revert data: a lock that was not a lock, stale write-back after a long walk, one failed case skipping the rest, per-event locking storms, locks and recents rows dropped on a move out of HOME or a delete and re-create, and no catch-up for recents, locks and shortcuts.

Daemon lifecycle faults: duplicate daemons, deleting another daemon's pid file, a stop blocked by the warm lock, no fallback when the watcher dies, a recycled pid blocking start-up, a destructive bashrc hook, an untrimmed log, and a start race in the alien daemon.
Only the recents daemon could be inspected or restarted and its version was kept in two hand-synced places. Now .dm.alien and .dm.alien.restart exist and one list holds both versions.
